cohort: Pregnant patients who underwent fetal MRI in the third trimester, including those whose delivery was complicated by shoulder dystocia (cases) and those with normal deliveries (controls), matched for maternal age, BMI, gestational diabetes, diabetes mellitus Type 1 or 2, gestational age at MRI examination, gestational age at birth, and birth weight.
finding: Higher fetal body volume and shoulder skin-to-skin distance, along with lower maternal obstetric conjugate, sagittal outlet diameter, coccygeal pelvic outlet, and maximal transverse diameter, were significantly associated with shoulder dystocia, with FBV, shoulder skin-to-skin distance, BPD, SOD, and MTD identified as independent predictors.
birth_weight: Matched between case and control groups.
gest_age: Matched between case and control groups (at MRI examination and at birth).
